<thought>We have the molecular formula C₁₆H₁₆O from the mass spectrum. To identify the correct structure among the possible isomers, the next inexpensive experiment is IR spectroscopy, which will reveal whether a carbonyl group is present (strong C=O stretch ~1700 cm⁻¹) or if the oxygen is only in an ether/alcohol (no strong carbonyl band). This will let us narrow the candidates quickly before any NMR simulations.</thought>
<final_answer>We need to obtain the IR spectrum of the sample to determine the functional group associated with the single oxygen atom (carbonyl vs. ether/alcohol). This will allow us to select the correct SMILES from the list of C₁₆H₁₆O isomers.
